name: Samoa
summary: Samoa taxes residents on worldwide income at up to 27%. Its capital gains tax (27%) applies only to capital assets held for three years or less; gains on assets held longer, and on foreign assets bought before becoming resident, are exempt. Dividends from Samoan companies are exempt, but foreign dividends are taxable at up to 27% with a foreign tax credit. No inheritance, gift or wealth tax was found.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents taxed on worldwide income (0/20/27%); CGT 27% only on assets held 3 years or less; Samoan dividends exempt.
regimes.eligibility: Resident individual: home in Samoa during the year, or present 183 days in any 12-month period beginning or ending in the year (Income Tax Act 2012 s. 6).

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains tax at 27% applies to a resident's net capital gain on disposal of capital assets anywhere, but gains on assets held for more than three years are exempt, as are gains on foreign (non-Samoan) assets acquired before becoming resident and on the principal residence. Cost is uplifted by 5% a year. For a long-term investor the rate is 0%.

sources.title: Income Tax Act 2012 (No. 21), including Part 4 Capital Gains Tax and Schedules 1-2
IR2 Individual Income Tax Return 2025 (rate table and capital gains box)

capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Income Tax Act 2012 s. 66(1): (a) assets acquired on or before 31 December 1989; (b) principal place of residence; (c) assets held for more than 3 years; (d) non-Samoan assets acquired before becoming resident; (f) estate disposals that would have been exempt for the deceased. s. 65(2): cost increased by 5% per annum.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: s. 63 and Schedule 1 para (8): CGT rate 27%. The 2025 IR2 return still asks 'Did you make a capital gain on an asset you bought and sold within three years?' at 27%. Gains on assets acquired for resale (s. 16(1)(b)) or held in a business are ordinary income at up to 27%.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Assumes holding periods over 3 years (guide: held longer than any holding period), so s. 66(1)(c) exempts the gain: 0 for all classes. Short-term (<= 3 years) gains: 27% with credit for foreign tax (s. 67).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: More than 3 years = exempt; 3 years or less = 27% CGT.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Net gains from assets acquired with the purpose of disposal at a profit are property income (s. 16(1)(b)) and business gains are business income, both at up to 27%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents' net capital gain includes worldwide disposals (s. 64(1)); foreign assets acquired before becoming resident are exempt (s. 66(1)(d)).
open_questions: The Act copy on the Ministry site is the 2012 text; later amendments (e.g. 2017) were not read, but the 2025 return confirms the 27% / 3-year rule.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by a resident (Samoan) company are exempt income (Schedule 2 Part A (1)(b)). Foreign dividends are property income of a resident (s. 16(1)(a)), taxed at the individual rates (27% above WST 25,000 per the 2025 return), with a foreign tax credit for foreign tax paid (s. 57).

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: Schedule 2 Part A (1)(b) exempts 'a dividend paid by a resident company' = 0. Foreign: top individual rate 27% on property income before the s. 57 foreign tax credit (credit limited to Samoan tax on that income).
dividends.withholding_outbound: Schedule 1 (4) lists non-resident WHT of 15% on interest, royalties and fees; dividends of resident companies are not in the list (no dividend WHT found).
dividends.treaty_network: No comprehensive tax treaty found; Samoa has 17 tax information exchange agreements and applies the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance (Ministry for Revenue). US dividends bear 30% US WHT, creditable up to the Samoan tax.
open_questions: Whether a resident individual's foreign dividends are ever taxed as 'business income' at a different rate was not examined.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets.

sources.title: Income Tax Act 2012 (No. 21), including Part 4 Capital Gains Tax and Schedules 1-2

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax was found among the taxes administered by the Ministry for Revenue. For CGT, transmission of an asset on death to the personal representative or a beneficiary is not a disposal giving rise to a gain (s. 73(1)(b)). A lifetime gift is a non-arm's-length disposal at market value (s. 74), which only matters for assets held 3 years or less.

sources.title: Income Tax Act 2012 (No. 21), including Part 4 Capital Gains Tax and Schedules 1-2

inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax found. A gift of an asset held 3 years or less can trigger 27% CGT on the market-value gain.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No Samoan transfer tax found on any assets.
open_questions: No official statement that Samoa has no estate or gift duty was found; absence inferred from the Ministry for Revenue's tax list and the Income Tax Act.
Stamp duty on transfers of land (if any) not researched.

residency.tax_residency_test: Income Tax Act 2012 s. 6: resident individual if the individual has a home in Samoa during the year, or is present for 183 days in any 12-month period commencing or ending in the tax year (part-year rules on arrival and departure).

corporate.summary: Company income tax 27% (Income Tax Act 2012 Schedule 1 (2)). Dividends from resident companies exempt. Samoa also has an international (offshore) companies regime, not researched.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets wherever they live; the app adds the federal layer. Where local tax on portfolio income is nil there is nothing to credit against US tax.
